findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in init worker goroutines
findings.body: Inside group.Go closures, `totalBatchesIndexed++` is an unsynchronized increment from multiple goroutines, and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigns to the outer `err` shared by all workers. These are data races. Init now runs at startup, with many namespaces and high concurrency, so the race is more likely to bite. The event count may also be wrong. Use an atomic counter and a local err.

findings.title: Init at construction runs before DB backend lifecycle and uses a cancelable server ctx
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, so the constructor blocks until all indexes are built, and any failure makes server creation fail outright. Also, the ctx passed to Init is the server-lifetime ctx (cancelled by Stop). It is also used for the search.init Watch goroutine; this is fine. But lifecycle.Init previously ran lazily after DI wiring, so the SQL backend now has to be fully usable at construction time. Callers constructing servers in tests or in non-storage targets will now eagerly hit the DB and may fail. The PR itself skips a postgres test because of this.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without lock
findings.body: BuildIndex now writes to b.cache under cacheMu only briefly, and concurrent builds are now possible. TotalDocs reads the map without taking cacheMu.RLock. This is a concurrent map read/write race and can panic. search.init now calls TotalDocs right after the concurrent builds, and the new logging call makes it more likely.

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex for same key can create duplicate/overwritten indexes
findings.body: Removing the function-wide lock means two concurrent builds for the same key (for example getOrCreateIndex from a search request racing with init or a watch event) both build and the last one silently overwrites the cache entry. For file-backed indexes, bleve.New on the same directory fails for the second builder, or leaks the earlier index, which is never closed.

findings.title: Trace context still not propagated in other methods
findings.body: Only GetResourceStats was fixed. WriteEvent, ReadResource and ListIterator still discard the span context with `_, span :=`, so child spans are not parented correctly. The same applies to bleve BuildIndex, which still uses `_, span`.
